Brazil’s former president Jair Bolsonaro is back in the hospital for abdominal pain, according to his son Carlos Bolsonaro.
Jair Bolsonaro has been hospitalized repeatedly over the years for abdominal issues, after he was stabbed in the stomach on the campaign trail in 2018.

Another day, another sea of placards spilling out onto Europe’s streets.
Protests continued in several European cities on Saturday after tens of thousands filled the continent’s cities on Friday in a youth-led day of action across more than 25 nations.
Student groups in the UK, France, Spain, Italy and beyond walked out on Friday over the sky-rocketing cost of living, rising tuition fees, underfunded education systems and what they cast as leaders’ complicity in Israel’s war in Gaza. In Italy, trade unions also joined the protests and called on their members to observe a nationwide strike.
Other grievances that have prompted Gen-Z-led protests this fall include high unemployment, the climate crisis and fears governments are failing to future-proof against unregulated artificial intelligenc...

Danish police averted an attempt by Russian intelligence services to assassinate a US-Ukrainian rapper in September ahead of a planned performance, police and security officials said on Friday.
Soon after the announcement, Denmark said it was expelling Russia’s defense attache in the country in protest, with Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen calling the alleged plot an unacceptable transgression.
“We don’t want to break off diplomatic relations with Russia in this particular situation that Denmark and Europe are in… But on the other hand, we want to send a very, very strong signal,” Rasmussen said.

item.description: Leaders from the United Kingdom and European Union are meeting for a landmark summit as British Prime Minister Andy Burnham pushes for a closer relationship with the bloc a decade after the Brexit vote.

item.title: UN top court finds Myanmar guilty of committing genocide against Rohingya minority
item.description: Myanmar committed genocide against the country’s long-persecuted Rohingya minority, the United Nations’ top court found Thursday, an unprecedented ruling that survivors of the atrocities have waited almost a decade to hear.

item.title: Analysis: For Xi and Putin, the Trump trilat was a win for a new world order
item.description: From an airy government villa in the hills of southern China on Friday emerged an image, perhaps, for our times: the leaders of China, Russia and the US standing shoulder-to-shoulder, proclaiming themselves the stewards of world peace.

item.title: Four men guilty of sex crimes against UK woman drugged by husband
item.description: Four British men were convicted on Thursday of raping or sexually abusing a woman who was drugged by her then-husband in a case with echoes of that of Gisele Pelicot, the French woman who became a global symbol in the fight against sexual violence.

item.title: Bridge connecting Russia to occupied Crimea has been hit again
item.description: The strategic Kerch Bridge, which connects Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula, has come under attack again, according to the Moscow-backed Crimea governor Sergei Aksyonov, soon after a part of it collapsed in a Ukrainian strike earlier this week.
